title: Credit Spread and PD from Spreads

maps.tested: Flagged by the sheet as potentially important within the Credit VaR reading, and carried on your formula card.
maps.specifics: Verify your card before the exam. It writes CS = (1/T) x ln(D/F) - Rf. The standard form is CS = -(1/T) x ln(D_t/F) - r, where D_t is the current market value of the debt. As written, the sign is inverted: precisely the polarity flip GARP builds distractors from. Also examinable: deriving PD from credit spreads (LO 30.c) and PD = (1/LGD) x (1 - (1 + r_f)/(1 + y)).

vardeezReading: CR-10: Very Important. "Credit Spread Risk can be imp too." CR-12: Important. LO 30.g (credit VaR) and LO 30.f (one-factor model) are important, LO 30.e relevant, the rest repeats to skim. CR-9: Very Important. "MOST IMP CHAPTER. Almost all LOs are imp here", with hazard rates, marginal and conditional probabilities and Merton expected, CDS to be left for a later reading.

selectors.name: Credit spread from market value of debt
selectors.what: Credit spread of zero-coupon debt from its market value Dt, face value F, maturity T and risk-free rate r with continuous compounding: CS = -(1/T) x ln(Dt/F) - r. The card's version (1/T) x ln(D/F) - Rf is inverted in sign and is the planted distractor.
selectors.theory: Why Dt = F x exp(-yT) gives the yield y = -(1/T) x ln(Dt/F), which is positive because Dt < F, and the spread is that yield less the risk-free rate; the -(1/T) x ln(Dt/F) alone is the yield, and forgetting 1/T reports a cumulative loss as an annual spread. Also a risky claim is discounted at the risk-free rate plus the T-year spread, f = fnd x exp(-(y - ynd) x T), and the Merton zero-coupon spread.

selectors.name: Derive PD from credit spreads
selectors.what: Default probability implied by spreads: average hazard rate lambda(T) = s(T)/(1 - R) (240 bps with R = 40% gives 4%), the bootstrapped forward hazard between two maturities, the interval PD for CVA from interpolated spreads, or the exact bond-price comparison of a risky and a risk-free bond.
selectors.theory: The spread is roughly an average loss rate, so dividing by LGD = 1 - R gives the hazard rate; this works well for CDS spreads and bonds near par; spread-implied PDs are risk-neutral, much higher than historical ones, and are used for valuation and CVA, not scenario analysis.

selectors.name: One-period PD from yield, recovery decides ranking
selectors.what: One-year PD = (1/LGD) x (1 - (1 + rf)/(1 + y)) = (y - rf)/((1 + y) x LGD), where LGD = 1 - R. Issuers are ranked by implied PD at given yields and recoveries, and the ranking can differ from the spread ranking.
selectors.theory: Pricing a one-year zero two ways, ((1 - PD) + PD x R)/(1 + rf) = 1/(1 + y), gives PD x LGD = 1 - (1 + rf)/(1 + y), the expected loss rate; at the same spread higher recovery means a higher implied PD, and dividing by R instead of LGD is the wrong-input trap.

selectors.name: Credit spread risk and its effect on credit VaR
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Credit spread risk' on CR-10 f; Map: 'credit spread risk' within the Credit VaR reading
selectors.what: Define credit spread risk (trading-book credit products move with spreads, so VaR or ES must capture spread changes) and assess its impact on credit VaR, as in the two-year zero with a spread change against default loss, or constant-level-of-risk rebalancing.

notSelected: CR-9 h beyond hazard rate from a spread (the definition and measures of credit spread, the risk-free rate used, the CDS-bond basis) and CR-9 j's comparison of historical with spread-implied hazard rates beyond S3 carry no shape, Map point or Vardeez pointer, and the Merton calculations of CR-9 l beyond the zero-coupon spread belong to A5.
